To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We applied whole exome sequence analysis to a cohort of 19 Saudi families with a single affected child.

we applied whole exomesequencing (WES) to identify de novo and inherited variants in Saudi families with autism spectrum disorder (ASDD), and that we found 47 variants, including 15 in ASD-candidate genes.

we performed whole exome sequencing on 19 triads with autism spectrum disorder from Saudi Arabia, and we identified 47 rare, deleterious variants in 15 autism candidate genes, including 10 that have not been implicated previously in autism spectrum disorder.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of ASD and the development of a novel analysis strategy to uncover de novo and inherited variants.
identifying rare ASD-associated variants in Saudi families and developing a computational pipeline for the analysis of WES data.
the discovery of new ASD candidate genes, and the development of an analytical framework that allows for the identification of de novo and/or inherited rare variants in ASD.

our findings provide evidence for the role of both de novo and rare inherited variants in ASD.
the genetic architecture of Saudi ASD patients is heterogeneous, and is characterized by both inherited and de novo rare variants, and that WES is an efficient tool to identify such variants.
the genetic architecture of autism spectrum disorder in the Saudi population is complex, heterogeneous, and private.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
WES can be used to detect rare deleterious variants, both de novo and transmitted, in families with ASD.
our study provides a unique resource of rare variants in ASD candidate genes, and our analysis pipeline is a useful tool for the identification of both de novo and transmitted rare variants in ASD.
the majority of the ASD cases are caused by de novo variants, while the remaining are caused by inherited rare variants, with some being autosomal recessive.

the majority of rare variants implicated in ASD in Saudi families are inherited and not de novo.
the majority of the variants we identified are inherited and not de novo, suggesting that the contribution of de novo mutations in ASD is not as high as expected.
